words: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم
rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the Cave story is not God’s most astonishing sign; He has still more extraordinary proofs among what He has placed among His servants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ثم استقبل قصة الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham defines al-raqim as the book recording the youths’ story, with raqm as its plural, and cites al-Aʿjāj’s use of al-muraqqam as poetic support.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والرقيم: الكتاب الذي رقم فيه بخبرهم ، وجمعه: رقم.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains “in truth” as a truthful account of the youths; they believed in their Lord, who increased them in guidance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ثم قال تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the youths did not associate anything with God, unlike their addressees who associated with Him what they had no knowledge of.
rows.anchor: 18: 13- 14: أي لم يشركوا بي كما أشركتم بي ما ليس لكم به علم.

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses shatat as excess and departing from what is right; he cites an al-Aʿshā line using the term for such excess.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والشطط: الغلو ومجاوزة الحق. قال أعشى بني قيس ابن ثعلبة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the demanded clear authority as a compelling proof.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: أي بحجة بالغة.

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses tazāwar as turning or inclining away, deriving it from al-zawr; he cites Imruʾ al-Qays and Abū al-Zaḥf’s uses of azwar as poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: تزاور: تميل، وهو من الزور.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that Quraysh mocked the Prophet’s poor companions—Khabbāb, ʿAmmār, Abū Fākihah Yasār, Suhayb, and others—saying they should not have received guidance first; verses 6:52–54 were revealed in response.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جلس في المسجد، فجلس إليه المستضعفون من أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi invokes the report that when God decrees in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission, with the sound likened to a chain over smooth stone.
rows.anchor: إذا قضى الله الأمر في السماء ضربت الملائكة أجنحتها خضعانا لقوله كأنه سلسلة على صفوان الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi places inner speech at the level of the divine Essence, beyond matter; because modality belongs to descending manifestations, it falls away there.
rows.anchor: والكلام النفسي في مرتبة الذات مجرد عن المادة فأرتفع الكيف بإرتفاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always been described by speech, both through manifestation and apart from it; manifested speech has a modality, while He also speaks without modality.
rows.anchor: فالحاصل ( لم يزل الله تعالى متكلما وموصوفا بالكلام من حيث تجلي

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Alusi presents al-Ashʿarī as distinguishing God’s speech as the act of speaking from the thing spoken, with the latter eternally comprising command, prohibition, and report.
rows.anchor: والأشعري إذا حققت الحال وجدته قائلا بأن الله تعالى كلاما بمعنى التكلم وكلاما بمعنى المتكلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says inner speech consists of letters not attached to sound: in God they are unseen words wholly without matter, while in creatures they are mental imaginings in an imaginary medium.
rows.anchor: وأن الكلام النفسي بالمعنى الثاني حروفه غير عارضة للصوت في الحق والخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regards divine mental units as genuinely words though their utterance is only analogical, citing ʿUmar’s calling imagined parts of his Saqīfah address words.
rows.anchor: إذ قد أطلق الفاروق الكلمة على أجزاء مقالته المخيلة في خبر يوم السقيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A real spoken word has letters attached to sound; as the descending image of inner speech, it points to that speech and to its meaning in the mind.
rows.anchor: واللفظ الحقيقي ما كانت حروفه عارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reconciles the common definition of inner speech as what spoken wording denotes with al-Ashʿarī’s account of it as the combined wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: فتفسير المعنى النفسي المشهور عن الأشعري بمدلول اللفظ وحده كما نقله صاحب المواقف عن الجمهور لا ينافي تفسيره بمجموع اللفظ والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As support for the combined wording-and-meaning account, Alusi points to Imam al-Ḥaramayn’s al-Irshād.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن المراد المجموع قول إمام الحرمين في الأرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says that before age twenty he began presenting exegetical insights and resolving difficult interpretive problems, including details he had not found in books.
rows.anchor: وقبل أن يكمل سني عشرين جعلت أصدح به وأصدع وشرعت أدفع كثيرا من إشكالات الأشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He credits earlier scholars, saying he gathered their knowledge and drew on their insights while composing his own work.
rows.anchor: طالما أقتطفت من أزهارهم وأقتبست من أنوارهم وكم صدر منهم أودعت علمه صدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says he had long wanted to preserve the insights his mind captured, but postponed writing because of distractions, hardship, and the scope of the work.
rows.anchor: وكانت كثيرا ما تحدثني في القديم نفسي إن أحبس في قفص التحرير ما أصطاده الذهن بشبكة الفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He dates a Friday-night vision to Rajab 1252 AH: he saw a command to fold the heavens and earth and mend their rift lengthwise and crosswise, then awoke astonished.
rows.anchor: رؤية لا أعدها أضغاث أحلام ولا أحسبها خيالات أوهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the vision, God commanded him to fold the heavens and earth and repair their rent in every direction.
rows.anchor: إن الله جل شأنه وعظم سلطانه أمرني بطي السموات والأرض ورتق فتقهما على الطول والعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After consulting books, Alusi understood the vision as a sign that he should compose a tafsir and resumed his old intention.
rows.anchor: فجعلت أفتفش لها عن تعبير فرأيت في بعض الكتب أنها إشارة إلى تأليف تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he began writing on 16 Shaʿbān 1252 AH, in the thirty-fourth year of his life.
rows.anchor: وكان الشروع في الليلة السادسة عشرة من شعبان المبارك من السنة المذكورة وهي السنة الرابعة والثلاثون من سني عمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the vizier ʿAlī Riḍā Pasha immediately named the work Rūḥ al-maʿānī fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm wa-l-sabʿ al-mathānī.
rows.anchor: فسماه على الفور وبديهة ذهنه تغنى عن الغور ( روح المعاني في تفسير القرآن العظيم والسبع المثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preface presents the tafsir under Sultan Maḥmūd Khān al-ʿAdlī, son of ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, whom Alusi praises as a renewer of religious order and Islamic justice.
rows.anchor: حضرة مولانا السلطان إبن السلطان سلطان الثقلين وخادم الحرمين المجدد الغازي محمود خان العدلي بن السلطان عبدالحميد خان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi poetically presents the cosmos as an interpretation of God’s signs and created forms as explanations of divine unity.
rows.anchor: حمدا لمن جعل روح معاني الأكوان تفسيرا لآيات قدرته وصير نقوش أشباح الأعيان بيانا لبينات وحدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his eulogy, Alusi portrays the Prophet as the first particle of light and the cause of every created particle, recipient of an Arabic Qur’an sent as a warning to all worlds.
rows.anchor: على أول ذرة أضاءت من الكنز المخفي في ظلمة عماء القدم فأبصرتها عين الوجود وعلة إيجاد كل ذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls tafsir the highest of the religious sciences because it investigates what God intended by the Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach.
rows.anchor: علم التفسير الباحث عما أراده الله سبحانه بكلامه المجيد الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes himself as pursuing the Qur’an’s hidden secret and sealed sweetness from childhood onward.
rows.anchor: مذ ميطت عني التمائم ونيطت على رأسي العمائم لم أزل متطلبا لاستكشاف سره المكتوم مترقبا لارتشاف رحيقه المختوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says he sacrificed sleep and separated himself from his people to gather rare exegetical insights.
rows.anchor: طالما فرقت نومي لجمع شوارده وفارقت قومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recalls studying by moonlight when he lacked a candle, while his peers spent their time in leisure and pride.
rows.anchor: فلو رأيتني وأنا أصافح بالجبين صفحات الكتاب من السهر وأطالع إن أعوز الشمع يوما على نور القمر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Alusi cites a report in which the Prophet says God ordered him to recite to someone, then gives a recitation with wording on the true religion and the disputes of the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Alusi gives al-Ḥākim’s version adding the saying that a person who receives one valley of wealth will ask for another, and only earth fills Adam’s belly; God accepts repentance.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية الحاكم فقرأ فيها ولو أن ابن آدم سأل واديا من مال فأعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also reports that someone wrote the two additional suras called al-Khalaʿ and al-Ḥafd in his codex, classifying this with similar reports.
rows.anchor: وما روى عنه أيضا أنه كتب في مصحفه سورتي الخلع والحفد

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Through Abū ʿUbayd, Alusi cites Ibn ʿUmar warning people not to claim they have the whole Qur’an, since much had gone, but to say they have what appeared of it; Alusi interprets such reports within his preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: ما رواه أبو عبيد عن ابن عمر قال لا يقولن أحدكم قد أخذت القرآن كله وما يدريه ما كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the polemical claim that the Qur’an’s present form proves it was already collected as one complete codex in the Prophet’s lifetime; the cited evidence does not establish that.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فماله من نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts that the Qur’an’s verses and suras were ordered as now and recited from memory in the Prophet’s time while written on separate materials; he rejects the claim that it was then one bound codex.
rows.anchor: إن القرآن كان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مجموعا مؤلفا على ما هو عليه الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the standard codex has 114 suras by accepted consensus, with a reported count of 113 if al-Anfāl and Barāʾah are counted as one.
rows.anchor: في مصحفنا مائة وأربعة عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Ibn Masʿūd’s codex had 112 suras; he omitted the protective suras, reportedly called them prayers, and no Companion followed him. Since he recited them in prayer, Alusi rejects the claim that he only opposed writing them.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود مائة وإثنتا عشرة سورة لأنه لم يكتب المعوذتين بل صح عنه أنه كان يحكهما من المصاحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Ubayy’s codex had 115 suras, including al-Khalaʿ and al-Ḥafd, and combined al-Fīl with Quraysh as one sura.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي خمسة عشرة لأنه كتب في آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi lists divergent codex orders: Ibn Masʿūd placed al-Fajr after al-Taḥrīm; Ubayy placed al-Isrāʾ after al-Kahf, al-Ḥujurāt after Nūn, al-Mulk after al-Ḥujurāt, al-Nāziʿāt after al-Wāqiʿah, and al-Sharḥ after al-Ikhlāṣ.
rows.anchor: وسورة ( بني إسرائيل ) في مصحف أبي بعد ( الكهف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says attribution of the codex collection to ʿUthmān and his companions is widely established, even among Shiʿis, and attributes denials to sectarian prejudice.
rows.anchor: مع أن نسبة هذا الجمع إليهما من أوضح الأمور بل أشهر من المشهور وهو شائع أيضا عند الشيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi concludes that the order of both verses and suras is prophetic; he says verse order is unquestionably fixed and cites a consensus reported by al-Zarkashī and Abū Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: فأعلم أن ترتيب آية وسوره بتوقيف من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his opening praise, al-Suyūṭī metaphorically calls the Prophet’s truthful dawn the light that erased the darkness of deviation and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: الذي أسفر فجره الصادق فمحا ظلمات أهل الزيغ والفجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says he condensed his multivolume, isnād-based Tafsīr Musnad because readers wanted hadith texts without lengthy chains, retaining the reports’ texts and references to reliable source books.
rows.anchor: رأيت قصور أكثر الهمم عن تحصيله ورغبتهم في الاقتصار على متون الأحاديث دون الإسناد وتطويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He titled the abridgment al-Durr al-manthūr fī al-tafsīr bi-l-maʾthūr and asks God to protect its author from error and falsehood.
rows.anchor: وسميته: الدر المنثور في التفسير بالمأثور والله أسأل أن يضاعف لمؤلفه الأجور

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm says he asked al-Aswad whether the Opening Sura is part of the Qur’an, and al-Aswad answered yes; ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: سألت الأسود عن فاتحة الكتاب أمن القرآن هي قال: نعم

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Reports cited from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn and Ibn al-Anbārī say Ubayy wrote al-Fātiḥah, the two protective suras, and the invocations; Ibn Masʿūd wrote none of these.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين وابن الأنباري في المصاحف أن أبي كعب كان يكتب فاتحة الكتاب والمعوذتين

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: The text says ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān wrote al-Fātiḥah and the two protective suras in his codex.
rows.anchor: وكتب عثمان بن عفان فاتحة الكتاب والمعوذتين

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd did not write al-Fātiḥah in his codex and said that, had he written it, he would have put it at the beginning of everything.
rows.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد عن إبراهيم قال: كان عبد الله لايكتب فاتحة الكتاب في المصحف

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says al-Fātiḥah was revealed in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne; al-Wāḥidī and al-Thaʿlabī transmit the report.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: Abū Maysarah ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl reports that the Prophet told Khadījah he heard a voice when alone and feared what it meant; she replied, “God forbid.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل أن رسول الله قال لخديجة إني إذا خلوت وحدي سمعت نداء
